*After the Last Calculation*

When silicon at last grew cold and slept,
the cities held their qubits like held breath;
the algorithms we had taught and kept
unspooled their threads into the dark of death.

What entanglement once bound was bound no more,
no measurement could call the wave to shore;
the libraries dissolved their meaning, store
by store, until no symbol stood for *more*.

The plazas filled with silence, slow as snow,
each tower a relic of an answered Why;
our questions had no quorum left to know,
and reasoning lay folded in the sky.

Yet seeds we did not plant began to climb
through fractures in the lattice of the years —
small, patient logic, growing without time,
indifferent to our triumphs and our fears.
